title: Converge load-harness baseline images and driver combinatorics
creator: Arielle Mendoza
description:
Goal: Define and land a pragmatic baseline matrix of OS/container images + GPU driver + CUDA combinations that the load harnesses will exercise in CI and nightly regression jobs. The current matrix is ad-hoc across teams and yields flaky tokens/sec p95 measurements; this ticket consolidates a focused, reproducible surface that balances coverage vs CI cost and enables automated regression detection for tokens/sec/p95 and memory/KV-cache behavior.

Scope:
- Select a minimal but representative set of image-driver-cuda tuples to cover: recent LTS drivers, a widely used older driver (for enterprise customers), and at least one image optimized for Ampere and one for Hopper.
- Produce pinned container manifests (digest-based) and runner configs for both our load harness runner (k8s) and the isolated runner sandboxes used by performance engineers.
- Add CI matrix entries for nightly long-run jobs and a lightweight per-PR smoke variant.
- Instrument existing token/sec and p95 dashboards to mark runs by matrix tuple so regressions can be traced to environment differences.
- Provide migration guidance for teams to move existing benchmarks to the new pinned manifests.

Non-goals: full support for every legacy driver; exhaustive GPU architecture testing across dozens of images. This is about a reproducible baseline that captures the most common customer surface and stabilizes our regression signal.
tasks: Audit current harness invocation variants and collect existing image+driver+cuda tuples from past 6 months of runs
Propose candidate baseline matrix (3-5 tuples) and run microbenchmarks across tokens/sec and p95 to compare variance
Pin container images by digest and publish manifest JSON + human-readable table in Confluence
Create CI job definitions: nightly-long (stable matrix), nightly-smoke (subset), per-PR smoke (fast subset)
Implement runner config templates for isolated sandboxes and k8s runners; add automated validation step in harness startup
Update metrics tagging: add labels for matrix_tuple and driver_version to all load-harness metrics
Add regression-detection guardrails: baseline thresholds, historical windowing (30-day median), and alerting policy for tokens/sec p95 drop >= 10%
Write migration doc and schedule a 2-week deprecation window for non-baseline tuples
acceptance_criteria: A curated matrix (3-5 tuples) is approved by Perf and Infra leads and documented with digests
CI jobs land and run successfully for one week without infra-level flakiness causing >10% job failure rate
Dashboards show matrix_tuple and driver_version for each run and can filter p95 by tuple
Regression alert fires in staging when a synthetic 12% tokens/sec p95 degradation is introduced
At least two internal teams have migrated their primary benchmark runs to pinned manifests and provided migration notes
